chapter: Leaving Hampton: Europe and Los Angeles
title: A New Year's Eve jam session with Batman and Carl Perkins
summary: Anthony Ortega took Monk to a Los Angeles house party jam where Carl Perkins played and Monk, with chops up, asked to sit in.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: But your name was associated with it by now.

It was associated with it, right. I went to a jam session on...It was Christmas, during the holiday, New Year's. Anthony Ortega, he was also in the band. I forgot about him. We called him "Batman." Batman was in the band, and he lived in Los Angeles. And when I got there, well naturally, he was kind of showing...He and Clifford Solomon lived in California, Los Angeles.

And we had talked about forming a group out of Hamp's band, within the band, after we left. And there was a jam session going on, and Batman said, 'I want you to come over to...' what was it, I forgot the little town they was having the jam session at. 'And there's a New Year's Eve party, and we can play, man, we can play.' And I'm anxious to do that because I need to meet the local musicians, find out what's happening, try to get in on it, in the clique or whatever.

And so I joined Batman for that New Year's Eve party. And I had my bass and my amp in the trunk of the car when we rode, in Batman's trunk. When we got there the house...it was in a house...was filled with people. A good time, like a party. And the music was just great, because guys was just playing. I mean the music was so powerful!

And I remember that Carl Perkins was playing piano. Carl's from my home town. And I felt comfortable about Carl being there because Carl was like, sort of a key figure. A great player, and knew all the tunes and everything.

And there was about three bass players. Myself, one bass in the corner, another bass playing, another guy playing upright...about three basses. And...but I wanted to play; I really wanted to play. I was hungry to play, really hungry to play.

Now, you got to realize, now I really got that instrument down. Because we did a lot of playing with the jazz cats in the band, that had nothing to do with Lionel Hampton's working. We would have jam sessions; we'd have all kinds of things where we would be constantly playing, and my chops were really up. My chops were really up in terms of speed and control over...I was...They were up from constant working and playing. I was ready to play and I was hungry to play.

And I asked one of the guys could I sit in. He said, 'Oh, yeah, man, come on it, yeah. Have the place. You can use my bass or there's so-and-so's bass over there.' I said, 'I got my own bass in the car.' He said, 'OK, fine. Bring it on in.'

In the meantime, I'm feeling comfortable with Carl Perkins there and meeting the other guys. I went out to the car and got my bass and when I come back in, it was understood that I was going to play the next set, after the break.
